title: Sample species key

credit.author: Sample written by Claude
credit.work: A stand-in in the shape of a key that goes to species, to try the screens. It is not John Wright's key.
credit.terms: Nobody's key. It goes from the app as soon as WrightFungusKey.json is put in Windfall/PrivateKeys.

footer: A sample, to show how a key that goes to species would work. Never eat a wild fungus on the word of a key.

steps.title: Spore print
steps.question: What colour is the spore print?
steps.help: Leave the cap gills down on paper that is half white and half black, under a bowl, overnight.

choices.text: A ring, and a bag at the base
choices.detail: Dig it up whole to see the bag

choices.text: A ring, in clumps on wood or roots
No ring, and the stem snaps like chalk

steps.title: Pink spores
steps.question: What colour are the cap and gills?

choices.text: Lilac to violet, in leaf litter
Grey-white to tan, large and fleshy
In tufts on wood, with a small ring
On the ground, with a cobweb veil when young
Tall and shaggy, turning to black ink
Rounded and white, gills pink then brown

results.name: Death cap
confirm: Greenish to olive cap, sometimes pale
White gills, free of the stem
A ring and a bag-like volva at the base
results.danger: Deadly. One cap can kill. Wash your hands after touching it.
results.verdict: Sample: the author's own verdict would show here, in his words, with his warnings.

results.name: Honey fungus
confirm: Black bootlace strands under the bark
results.danger: Look-alikes on wood include the deadly funeral bell.
results.garden: A serious killer of trees and shrubs. Dig out and remove infected roots and stumps.
results.verdict: Sample: the author's own verdict would show here, in his words, with his warnings.

results.name: Charcoal burner
confirm: Cap a mix of purple, green and grey
Gills feel greasy and bend without snapping
results.verdict: Sample: the author's own verdict would show here, in his words, with his warnings.

results.name: Wood blewit
confirm: Lilac to violet cap and gills when young
Late autumn in leaf litter and compost heaps
results.danger: Webcaps can look much the same. Their spores are rusty brown, so take a print.
results.garden: Often found on old compost and leaf mould heaps.
results.verdict: Sample: the author's own verdict would show here, in his words, with his warnings.

results.name: Livid pinkgill
results.danger: Poisonous. A cause of serious stomach upsets.
results.verdict: Sample: the author's own verdict would show here, in his words, with his warnings.

results.name: Sheathed woodtuft
confirm: Two-toned cap that dries from the middle
results.danger: Very like the deadly funeral bell, which grows in the same places.
results.verdict: Sample: the author's own verdict would show here, in his words, with his warnings.

results.name: Webcaps
confirm: Cobweb veil between cap and stem when young
results.danger: Some webcaps are deadly and the damage can show days later. They are hard to tell apart.

results.name: Shaggy inkcap
confirm: Tall white cap with shaggy scales
Often on disturbed ground and new lawns

results.name: Field mushroom
confirm: No yellow stain when the base is cut
results.danger: The yellow stainer looks similar and is poisonous. Its base turns bright yellow when cut.
